title: Staged Capacity Gate Calendar & Cross-Surface Sync Playbook
creator: Aisha Romero
description: Purpose: Create a single-source playbook and calendar for coordinating staged capacity gates across runtime, Console, and API surfaces to reduce cross-team contention during multi-surface launches. Scope: - Define capacity gate windows (reserve/hedge) per region and feature lane. - Standardize signal definitions (canary-green, ramp-10, hedge-guard). - Specify cutover checklist for Runtime, Console dashboards, and API schema changes. - Provide escalation and rollback triggers tied to latency/CQ percentiles and error budget status. Goals: - Avoid double-booking of capacity-heavy launches across surfaces. - Reduce last-minute rollbacks due to uncoordinated canaries. - Provide automated calendar signals and a small ops runbook for the week-of-go-live. Out of scope: infra procurement, long-term capacity forecasting models (tracked separately).
acceptance_criteria: A single calendar (GCal + internal LaunchHub view) reflects capacity gates with owner & region metadata
A minimal runbook with play-by-play (preflight, canary, ramp, hedge, rollback) published to Confluence
Auto-generated calendar alerts (48h, 6h, 1h) and a Slack channel for the launch corridor are wired
Cross-surface preflight checklist has signed owners from Runtime, Console, and API teams
Canary success/failure thresholds and automatic fallback policy are documented and linked to runtime alerting dashboards

risks: Insufficient buy-in from external platform teams could leave calendar gaps
Automating alerts too aggressively may create noise and desensitize on-call
Edge cases where console dashboard changes are content-only but still require capacity (e.g., large dashboard JSON payloads)
Regional capacity constraints (APAC spots) may require manual overrides during holiday weeks
notes: Design decision: use a conservative default hedge (20% reserved for first 48h) — this can be tuned per feature lane
Trade-off: lean automation now vs more complete scheduler later. Prioritizing a lightweight set of signals to reduce implementation time
Coordination pattern: adopt a single ‘launch corridor’ Slack channel per week-of-go-live and a named runbook owner for 72h post-launch
